title: Allocative shadow budgeting: GPU constraint scan
summary: A simulation worksheet to test headcount and credit allocation tradeoffs when GPU capacity is the binding constraint. Focuses on: (1) reserve vs burst credit carveouts; (2) FTE vs contractor hiring mixes; (3) pricing sensitivity when applying token-price changes or quantization savings. Designed to produce quick gating thresholds for finance + infra decisions ahead of Q3 planning.
assumptions: Baseline ARR growth path = 42% YoY for product-led cohort
Average monthly GPU hours per 1k tokens = 0.28 GPU-hours (unoptimized)
Credits can cover up to 15% of gross GPU spend in contract year
Contractors deliver 60% of FTE throughput on average for inference infra work

sensitivity_analysis_notes: Summary of scenario runs: Baseline uses steady reserves and planned hires. Scenario B reduces gross GPU spend by drawing credit reserve (max 15%) which lowers token unit cost ~15% but consumes contractual credit buffer; triggers: if customer take-rate >+25% for 6 weeks, stop draw. Scenario C models unexpected demand surge mitigated via contractors: contractors bridge 6 months of capacity with 40% higher per-unit labor cost and 30% longer onboarding latency; net monthly opex increases but avoids 3 months of reserved GPU commit. Scenario D assumes adoption of 4-bit quantization on 2 heavy models (25% perf degradation on tail but 45% compute save) — largest benefit to token unit cost and headcount reallocation (can defer 2 infra hires). Key gating thresholds captured below: if price per token rises >12% QoQ, reprioritize burst credits to preserve SLA; if latency SLO breaches 1.5x baseline, open a dedicated capacity procurement RFP.
conclusions: The blended view shows using credits aggressively (Scenario B) improves short-term unit economics but increases downside operational risk if demand keeps rising. Contractor-first surge (Scenario C) is viable for temporary spikes but not sustainable beyond 3 quarters. Quantization (Scenario D) yields the best long-term delta in budget headroom and should be piloted on non-critical models immediately.
